## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75 (*Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa-asammata*) establishes that a nun who has completed the required twelve years of seniority but confers ordination without receiving formal authorization from the Saṅgha commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. As with the preceding rule (Pācittiya 74), the background narrative addresses situations where pupils remain foolish and uninstructed because their ordaining teacher (*pavattinī*) lacks competence [Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. Under this regulation, a nun must be capable and modest (*byattā lajjinī*), rather than incompetent or shameless (*bālā alajjinī*), to receive permission to train disciples [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken highlights that whereas a monk is not required to seek formal communal certification of his competence to ordain others, a nun must be formally granted the "agreement to ordain" (*vuṭṭhāpanasammuti*) by the Community [Hüsken 1997]. Linguistically, as Sujato observes, the text employs the causative noun *vuṭṭhāpanasammuti* to denote the Saṅgha's agreement empowering the preceptor to confer ordination, distinguishing it from the non-causative *vuṭṭhānasammuti* requested by a candidate [Sujato 2009].

SuttaCentral identifies full parallels in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 75) and *Parivāra* (Pc 75), along with Vinaya lineages across other early Buddhist schools: Dharmaguptaka (Bi-Vb Pc 132), Sarvāstivāda (Bi-Vb Pc 107), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Bi-Vb Pc 107), Mahāsāṅghika (Bi-Vb Pc 94), and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* (Pc 94) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 121 texts, primarily sharing legal and narrative formulas with adjacent Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga ordination rules (notably Pc 73, Pc 67, Pc 72, Pc 64, Pc 63, and Pc 74) and Khandhaka sections on community transactions (Kd 15, Kd 20, Kd 13, and Kd 14) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records strong cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga*, where DharmaNexus and SuttaCentral concur on the shared cross-tradition heritage of this ordination regulation [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
